title: Songwriters at 1600 Broadway and Whiting's temper
summary: Writers like Frank Loesser and Johnny Burke gathered daily at a publisher's at 1600 Broadway; Whiting's Irish temper hurt his standing on the coast.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: There are times in the songwriting business that you have a desire to write something, and

That's one of the darndest frustrations for a person to have, who is writing that particular, I'd say, form for a living --and at one time, that was all I had to do, to write. Because I can tell you the time -- at 1600 Broadway, when a very, very fine friend who went on to bigger things -- Frank Lesser -- and all the big groups, Johnny Burke, all of them, we all congregated at Will Wontillis' at 1600 Broadway, every day. All the songwriters were there trashing around, well, what did you do yesterday? Did you get any consideration from him? Is he in a good mood? What's the best time to see him -- in the morning or in the evening?

But we all got together and thrashed out what was done the day before, and a lot of times, it would help a lot of writers, you see. So Mr. Gys and Dolls, he was there, just an ordinary guy like we were, until he hit the bucket up there, and when that came, he was gone - he was on his own. When Johnny Burke hit it, he was gone.
We would have had a chance -- George and Nat and myself, out there, with those fellows, if -- see, George had an awful temper, not 100% --but 1000% Irish, with an
Irish temper, and he had been to the coast and was back in New York, and that's how I met him.
But he didn't leave too good of a taste in a lot of the cats' mouths out there because of his temper.
